# A two-limb number from its limbs

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `make_2_limbs` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The two-limb number with the value $y$, exactly:

$$x = y.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $y = h + l$, $x = x_0 + x_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from_limbs(p)` | `T*` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | `Expansion<T, 2>::from_limbs(p)`, with `p` pointing to the two limbs; checked when `KAIRN_CHECKS` is 1 |
| `from_limbs_unchecked(p)` | `T*` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | the same, never checked |
| `from_limbs(p)` | `T*` | `Interval<T, 2>` | `Interval<T, 2>::from_limbs(p)`, `p` pointing to the limbs as they were read (the bounds' or the center's, then the radius); the limbs of a canonical set, checked when `KAIRN_CHECKS` is 1; the round trip gives every limb back but the sign of a zero and the payload of a NaN ([One enclosure interface](enclosure.md#limbs)); each bound through `make_2_limbs`; `constexpr`; rounds (the test of a canonical bound), and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode |
| `from_limbs(p)` | `T*` | `Ball<T, 2>` | `Ball<T, 2>::from_limbs(p)`, `p` pointing to the limbs as they were read (the bounds' or the center's, then the radius); the limbs of a canonical set, checked when `KAIRN_CHECKS` is 1; the round trip gives every limb back but the sign of a zero and the payload of a NaN ([One enclosure interface](enclosure.md#limbs)); the center through `make_2_limbs`, the radius through `make_2`; `constexpr`; rounds (the test of a canonical center), and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode |
| `Expansion<T, 2>(r)` | `SumAndError<T>` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | explicit: the result `r` of `two_sum` or `fast_two_sum` as the pair (`r.sum`, `r.error`), through `from_limbs_unchecked`; canonical, of value $a + b$ exactly, when both members are finite, which a debug build checks ([`two_sum_entry`](two_sum_entry.md) says when) |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED (a constructor does not take it).

## Requires

- $y$ is canonical: finite and normalized, or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$, or $(\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $x$ is canonical and is $y$ exactly: when $y$ is finite, $x$ is finite and normalized with $x_0 + x_1 = y$; when $y = \pm\infty$, $x = (\pm\infty, 0)$; when $y$ is a NaN, $x = (\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `make_2_limbs_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeMake.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeMake.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions make_2_limbs_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `make_2_limbs_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/make_2_limbs.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/make_2_limbs.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# from_limbs: the 2-limb number with the limbs (h, l) the program gives, which must be canonical;
# each limb guarded (rule R3; milestone1.md, "Values that enter from the program").

x0 = guard(h)
x1 = guard(l)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#make_2_limbs)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 110 400 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 110 400 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 6 159 386 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand, supplementary run: 1 domain of 1 format | 248 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
